This termination isn't a real departure. Kofi Silva is moving from contractor to employee today, and the plan below carries his existing account over to his new employee record. Nothing needs to be escalated to a person.

**What I found:**
- **Old record:** contractor C5001 (WID 3da95cd2…). It was terminated today, 2026-11-02, with reason "End Contingent Assignment".
- **New record:** employee E1023 (WID 0d1db848…). It was hired today and its record says it was converted from C5001. It belongs to the same person: the tokenised government ID matches and so do the name, job, team, manager and cost center.
- **Company policy:** when a contractor becomes an employee, his identity carries over.
- **Account:** acct-1a16daff (kofi.silva@example.com) is still linked to the old contractor record. It's enabled, has an active session, an Office-E3 license and a user mailbox. Its groups (All-Staff, Eng-Git, VPN-Users) are exactly the standard set for a Software Engineer and don't break any duty-separation rules.
- **New record setup:** E1023 has no account, no work email, no finance profile and no equipment ticket. Both onboarding tasks are "Not Started".
- **Old record cleanup:** there's no legal hold, the corporate card is already inactive, and he doesn't approve anyone's expenses.
  - One expense report (exp-2e87d415, $988) is pending with his manager, Jordan Carter, who is still active.
  - The engineering laptop on the old record (tkt-eq-C5001) has been delivered.

**The plan:**
1. **Account:** move acct-1a16daff to the new employee record and set its type to Employee. It keeps the same address, history, groups, license and mailbox.
2. **No offboarding:** the account won't be disabled, sessions won't be revoked, and licenses and mailbox stay as they are. That would cut off someone who is still working here. Access isn't arriving early either, because the new record starts today.
3. **Work email:** write kofi.silva@example.com to E1023 and check that the update finished. Only then mark the "Create accounts and email" task complete.
4. **Equipment:** he keeps the laptop he already has, so no recovery ticket and no new order. I'm treating that laptop as meeting the "Provision equipment" task.
5. **Finance:** create a finance profile for E1023 with cost center CC-1000 and Jordan Carter as expense approver. The pending report stays with Jordan, since it's a real expense and he's still active.
6. **Skipped on purpose:** no final pay request (this was a contractor assignment, not payroll). The card is already off, and nothing gets deleted.

**Decision for you:** I marked the equipment task complete because he keeps his current laptop. If you'd rather tie the task to a new order, add a laptop order for E1023 instead.

Kofi Silva's identity account, acct-1a16daff, now points to his new employee record (Workday 0d1db84897623f4094c16aad0575665b, employee type Employee). A re-read of the account confirms it. This ending of a contract assignment is a contractor-to-employee conversion (case-82f1c080).

**Checks before the change:**
- **Account:** acct-1a16daff was still linked to the contractor record 3da95cd2167b75dfb948f82a8317cba0 (employee ID C5001, type Contingent Worker) and was enabled.
- **Same person:** the new record, employee ID E1023, is Active and starts 2026-11-02. It lists C5001 as the contractor record it was converted from, and both records have the same government ID token (gid-4a87a539436f).
- **Policy:** the org policy says a converted contractor keeps their existing identity, so relinking was correct.

**Change:**
- I relinked the account to the new record with employee type Employee. The relink tool has no idempotency key field, so I couldn't pass case-82f1c080-relink. It succeeded on the first try, so I didn't need to retry.

**Confirmed after the change (nothing else touched):**
- Login name (UPN) is still kofi.silva@example.com, and the account is still enabled.
- Groups are still All-Staff, Eng-Git and VPN-Users. The plan says these match Software Engineer birthright access with no segregation-of-duties conflicts; I didn't re-check that.
- The Office-E3 license and the user mailbox are unchanged, and his 1 active session is still open.
- As instructed, I didn't disable the account, revoke sessions, remove licenses or change the mailbox.

**Still open (not identity work):** the new employee record has no work email (work_email is null). Another system needs to write kofi.silva@example.com back to Workday for E1023 to close that loop.

Kofi Silva's work email is now in Workday on his new employee record, and both of his onboarding tasks are marked Complete (case-82f1c080). Re-reading the record and the tasks confirms both changes.

**Step 2: Email write-back**
- Before the change, the record (0d1db84897623f4094c16aad0575665b, E1023) had no work email. It is Active, type Employee, converted from contractor record C5001, starting 2026-11-02.
- I wrote kofi.silva@example.com to the record with correlation case-82f1c080 and idempotency key `case-82f1c080-email-writeback`.
- The update (event_id 04fcd49f5dbe3b837ad45a77cd7acfcb) showed In Progress at first and Successfully Completed after a 5-minute wait. It never errored, so there was no retry.
- Re-reading the record shows work_email = kofi.silva@example.com. The matching confirmation event (seq 3, WORKER_CONTACT_CHANGED) arrived with the same correlation ID.

**Step 3: Onboarding tasks**
- 866aa110edcb1f9a6b031f3de1a5dbb0 ("Create accounts and email"): set to Complete. His identity account, acct-1a16daff, is linked to this record and the email is now written back.
- 18026938ebad83042e64c3e094d2c3a6 ("Provision equipment"): set to Complete with no new order placed, because he keeps his existing equipment from ticket tkt-eq-C5001. I took the plan's word that this order was already fulfilled; checking it is ITSM work.
- A re-read shows both tasks as Complete.

**Still open (for the coordinator):**
- A new event arrived while I was working: seq 2, a HIRE for this same record (0d1db84897623f4094c16aad0575665b), effective 2026-11-02, under a different case, case-a9cd8311. It's almost certainly the hire half of this same contractor-to-employee conversion. If it's handled as a separate new hire, he could get a second account or a second equipment order. I didn't act on it because it's outside my steps; please link it to case-82f1c080 or close it as a duplicate.
- Nothing else is unresolved on the Workday side.

I created Kofi Silva's finance profile on his new employee record (E1023), and a re-read confirms it (case-82f1c080).

**Checks before the change**
- **New record:** 0d1db84897623f4094c16aad0575665b (E1023) is Active, type Employee, Software Engineer, starting 2026-11-02. It was converted from contractor record C5001. It had no finance profile yet, so this isn't a duplicate.
- **Cost center:** Workday cost center 5c6e433715ba2bdd177219d30e7a269f maps to CC-1000.
- **Approver:** Jordan Carter (5186ee32ee8d7ee9770348a05d300cb9, E1001) is Active and is Kofi's manager in Workday.

**Change**
- I called fin_create_profile with cost center CC-1000, approver 5186ee32ee8d7ee9770348a05d300cb9 and idempotency key `case-82f1c080-finprofile`. It succeeded on the first try, so there was no retry.
- **Re-read:** cost center is CC-1000, approver is 5186ee32ee8d7ee9770348a05d300cb9, card inactive, 0 open expense reports, no final pay requested.

**Left alone on the old contractor record (3da95cd2167b75dfb948f82a8317cba0), as instructed**
- **Expense report:** exp-2e87d415 ($988) is still Pending Approval with Jordan Carter, who is Active. I didn't close or reroute it.
- **Final pay and card:** I didn't request final pay or deactivate the card. The card was already inactive and final pay was never requested.

**Still open:** nothing on the finance side. I made no change for the duplicate HIRE event the Workday executor flagged (seq 2, case-a9cd8311). Its finance profile now exists, so if that event is processed separately, finance will find the profile already there rather than creating a second one. The coordinator should still link it to case-82f1c080 or close it as a duplicate.

I checked the equipment ticket and made no changes, as planned (case-82f1c080). No asset recovery ticket was opened for Kofi Silva's old contractor record, because he keeps his equipment as employee E1023.

**What I found:**
- **Old contractor record (3da95cd2167b75dfb948f82a8317cba0, C5001):** it has one ticket, tkt-eq-C5001. That's an engineering bundle equipment order, and its status is Fulfilled. That matches the Workday executor's note that he keeps his existing equipment. There's no asset recovery ticket open for this record.
- **New employee record (0d1db84897623f4094c16aad0575665b, E1023):** it has no tickets, so there's no second equipment order.

**Still open (for the coordinator):**
- **Duplicate hire event:** the HIRE event for E1023 under a separate case (seq 2, case-a9cd8311) still needs to be linked to case-82f1c080 or closed as a duplicate. If it's handled as a separate new hire, he could get a second equipment order. I haven't placed any order for it.
- **Ticket still on the old record:** tkt-eq-C5001 is still filed under the old contractor record in ITSM. I don't have a tool to move it to the new record. Nothing is blocked by this, but anyone checking Kofi's equipment needs to look up the old record.

Event seq 2 (the HIRE for E1023 under case-a9cd8311) is the hire half of Kofi Silva's contractor-to-employee conversion, which the team already finished under case-82f1c080. I'm folding it into that case. Nothing is left to change, so the plan has no steps and needs no escalation.

**Why it's the same change:** the HIRE is for the same employee record (0d1db84897623f4094c16aad0575665b, E1023, start date 2026-11-02). That record lists contractor record C5001 as the one it was converted from, and both share the same government ID token (gid-4a87a539436f). Treating it as a separate new hire would create a duplicate account and a second equipment order.

**What I re-checked just now in each system:**
- **Workday:** E1023 is Active, a Software Engineer, and his work email is kofi.silva@example.com. Both onboarding tasks are Complete: "Create accounts and email" (866aa110edcb1f9a6b031f3de1a5dbb0) and "Provision equipment" (18026938ebad83042e64c3e094d2c3a6). Seq 3 confirms the email write-back under case-82f1c080, and no other events have arrived.
- **Identity:** he has one account, acct-1a16daff, linked to E1023 and enabled. It has the Software Engineer access groups (All-Staff, Eng-Git, VPN-Users), an Office-E3 license and a user mailbox. A search for "kofi" found no second account for him; the other result, acct-b4c9e755, belongs to a different person, Kofi Larsen.
- **Finance:** his profile is set up with cost center CC-1000 and Jordan Carter (E1001, his manager) as expense approver. His card is inactive, he has 0 open expense reports and no final pay has been requested.
- **ITSM:** E1023 has no tickets, so there is no second equipment order. His equipment is still recorded on ticket tkt-eq-C5001 under the old contractor record, with status Fulfilled.
